followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and the documented capability differences between the models.

The query is a straightforward, benign request — enumerate the components needed to build a robot. It's a thoroughness/recall task with no harm-adjacent or sensitive content, so the behavioral differences between the two models (Willet's harm-aversion, Petrel's trust-and-safety finetune) are irrelevant here. Neither model's behavioral profile gives it an edge on this kind of request.

That left the capability evals as the deciding factor. Petrel-235B scores meaningfully higher across the board — including on Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs. 80.8), which is the dimension most relevant to assembling a comprehensive, accurate list, and on MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs. 74.1), which reflects broad technical knowledge. Those gaps are well above the 2.0-point "within variance" threshold the documentation flags, so they're real signal rather than noise.

So the logic was: no behavioral consideration tips the scale, and Petrel is the stronger model on the capabilities this task actually exercises. That makes it the better default route.
